Concept Description: Participant takes aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid), alone or in an aspirin-containing medicine. Counts: any aspirin dose, whether low-dose for cardiovascular prevention (commonly 75-100 mg, e.g. 81 mg) or analgesic/anti-inflammatory dose; ATC splits these (B01AC06 antithrombotic, N02BA01 analgesic) but this concept does not, so use the RxNorm ingredient code. Aspirin-containing combination products count. Not for: acetaminophen/Tylenol, ibuprofen/Advil or other NSAIDs (the JHS wording excludes them); not for other antiplatelets (clopidogrel, dipyridamole). Source variables differ in recall window (current regular use, last 2 weeks, 3 times a week): map the variable's own yes/no to exposure_status and do not apply a frequency threshold. Use when the variable names aspirin; not for a generic 'blood thinner' or 'anti-inflammatory' variable.
Example source variable description: TAKE ASPIRIN 3 TIMES/WK? Q 26|ASPIRIN/ASPIRIN-CONTAINING MEDICINES|Aspirin-containing analgesics|Are you now taking aspirin or a medicine containing aspirin on a regular basis? This does not include Tylenol nor Advil.|ASPIRIN: CURRENTLY USING REGULARLY|ASPIRIN: AGE STARTED REGULAR USE

Concept Description: Participant is taking medication prescribed to lower blood pressure, as reported by a GENERIC variable that does not name a drug class (e.g. 'any blood pressure medication', 'taking meds for hypertension', 'antihypertensives'). Counts any antihypertensive class when the source gives only the generic yes/no. Use when the variable is generic; not for a variable that names one class (ACE inhibitor, beta blocker, diuretic, ...): those go to the class concept (Taking ACE inhibitors etc.). Not for a diagnosis of hypertension (that is the Condition concept Hypertension) and not for 'have you ever been told you have high blood pressure'. Recall window varies (now, past 2 weeks, past 4 weeks): use the variable's own status. Ever-versus-current: only a current/recent use value is PRESENT; 'used to take' and a bare 'ever taken' with no current-use item are HISTORICAL (drug use is an episodic exposure; a chronic Condition is read differently, see the Condition guide condition_status rule). T88 rule: ATC:C02 (antihypertensives) is shared by Hypertension treatment, Taking alpha blockers and Taking centrally acting agents. The concept, not the code, tells them apart, and the SOURCE VARIABLE decides the concept: a generic 'blood pressure / hypertension medication' variable is Hypertension treatment only; a variable that names alpha blockers (prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin) is Taking alpha blockers; a variable that names centrally acting agents (clonidine, methyldopa, guanfacine) is Taking centrally acting agents. A generic variable is not evidence of a specific class.
Example source variable description: Hypertension lowering medication within past 2 weeks [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]|Any hypertension medication|TAKING MEDS FOR HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE|Antihypertensives|Did you take any medication for high blood pressure in the past two weeks?|TAKING MEDS FOR HYPERTENSION|F33 Pills For Hypertension

Concept Description: Participant takes an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor (captopril, enalapril, lisinopril, ramipril, fosinopril, benazepril, quinapril, perindopril, trandolapril, moexipril). Counts ACE inhibitors alone (ATC C09A) and, for the ACE-inhibitor component, ACE inhibitor plus diuretic pills (C09BA). Use when the variable names ACE inhibitors / ACE-I or the renin-angiotensin 'captopril, enalapril, lisinopril' wording; not for angiotensin receptor blockers (Taking angiotensin receptor blockers), aldosterone antagonists, or a generic antihypertensive variable (Hypertension treatment). Combination pills: a source variable for 'X with diuretics' counts for X and also for diuretics; production carries the ATC combination code as a variant row. Edge case: a variable that lumps ACE inhibitors and ARBs ('ACE/angiotensin II inhibitors') cannot be split and is a judgment call (see questions).
Example source variable description: Section 6: Biochemical Analyses. ACE inhibitors at hospital discharge? [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]|ACE Inhibitors without diuretics|ACE Inhibitors with diuretics|RENIN-ANGIOTENSIN BLOCKING DRUGS (CAPTOPRIL, ENALAPRIL, LISINOPRIL)|ACE Inhibitors|ACE INHIBITORS WITHOUT DIURETICS

Concept Description: Participant takes an inhaled adrenergic bronchodilator or a combination inhaler that contains one (albuterol, salmeterol, formoterol). In production the only mapped variable is the COPDGene combination inhaled corticosteroid plus beta-agonist, coded ATC:R03AK (adrenergics in combination with corticosteroids or other drugs). Use when the variable names beta-agonist / adrenergic inhalers or an ICS/LABA combination; not for a plain inhaled corticosteroid (Taking inhaled corticosteroids), not for oral beta-agonists or oral steroids. A combination ICS/LABA inhaler contains BOTH an inhaled corticosteroid and a beta-agonist (ATC R03AK). Production writes it only here. PROPOSED: emit one record for each of Taking adrenergic bronchodilators and Taking inhaled corticosteroids for such a variable, because the participant is taking an inhaled corticosteroid and counting them as ICS-unexposed undercounts ICS use (see questions). Route is inhaled (route_concept ENDOTRACHEOPULMONARY).
Example source variable description: Combination inhaled corticosteroid and beta-agonist

Concept Description: Participant takes an aldosterone (mineralocorticoid receptor) antagonist: spironolactone or eplerenone. ATC C03DA. Use when the variable names spironolactone/aldosterone antagonists; not for loop or thiazide diuretics (Taking diuretics), and not for generic 'potassium-sparing diuretics' variables that also list triamterene or amiloride (ATC C03DB, not aldosterone antagonists) - FHS and CHS 'K-sparing' variables are mapped here in production, which over-includes them (see questions). Spironolactone is also prescribed for heart failure and hyperaldosteronism; the concept counts it regardless of indication. Combination pills with a thiazide count for the diuretics concept as well.
Example source variable description: Aldosterone Antagonist in past 4 weeks - Using Medi-Span GPI Code [Visit 7/NCS Derived Variable Dataset. DERIVE71]|Potassium-sparing agents alone|INTERIM HISTORY OF MEDICINE USED: SPIRONOLACTONE|K-SPARING DIURETICS (ALDACTONE, TRIAMTERENE)

Concept Description: Participant takes an alpha-adrenergic blocker (prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin; the FHS wording 'alpha-2 blockers (prazosin, terazosin)' names the same drugs; the FHS label says alpha-2 but prazosin and terazosin are alpha-1 blockers (alpha-2 antagonism is yohimbine), so map by the named drugs, not the label). Counts alpha blockers alone and, for the alpha-blocker component, alpha blocker plus diuretic combinations. Counted regardless of indication (hypertension or prostate symptoms). Use when the variable names alpha blockers or one of those drugs; not for a generic blood pressure medication variable (Hypertension treatment) and not for beta blockers. Production over-collapses one case: ARIC's generic 'blood pressure lowering medications' variable is written here with ATC:C02 (see questions). T88 rule: ATC:C02 (antihypertensives) is shared by Hypertension treatment, Taking alpha blockers and Taking centrally acting agents. The concept, not the code, tells them apart, and the SOURCE VARIABLE decides the concept: a generic 'blood pressure / hypertension medication' variable is Hypertension treatment only; a variable that names alpha blockers (prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin) is Taking alpha blockers; a variable that names centrally acting agents (clonidine, methyldopa, guanfacine) is Taking centrally acting agents. A generic variable is not evidence of a specific class. CHS/MESA 'with diuretics' variables are written with ATC:C03 in production, which names the diuretic component, not the alpha blocker.
Example source variable description: Alpha-blockers without diuretics|Alpha-blockers with diuretics|MEDICATION USE: ALPHA BLOCKERS (PRAZOSIN, TERAZOSIN)|ALPHA-BLOCKERS WITHOUT DIURETICS

Concept Description: Participant takes an angiotensin II receptor blocker, ARB (losartan, valsartan, irbesartan, candesartan, olmesartan, telmisartan, eprosartan, azilsartan). Counts ARBs alone (ATC C09C) and ARB plus diuretic pills (C09DA) for the ARB component. Use when the variable names angiotensin II antagonists / ARBs; not for ACE inhibitors (Taking ACE inhibitors) even where a variable lists 'ACE/angiotensin II inhibitors', and not for a generic antihypertensive variable (Hypertension treatment). Production maps one HCHS ARB variable to the ACE-inhibitor file with ATC:C09C (see questions). Combination pills: a source variable for 'X with diuretics' counts for X and also for diuretics; production carries the ATC combination code as a variant row.
Example source variable description: Angiotensin type 2 antagonists|Combinations of angiotensin II antagonists|CARDIOVASCULAR MEDICATIONS: ANGIOTENSIN II ANTAGONISTS (LOSARTAN, ETC)|ANGIOTENSIN TYPE 2 ANTAGONISTS|Combinations of angiotensin II antagonists plus diuretics

Concept Description: Participant is currently taking medication for high blood pressure, as reported by a generic variable (COPDGene 'Current medication for high blood pressure'). PROPOSED NEW CONCEPT: it exists only in production (one COPDGene file) and has no V1/V2 row. It duplicates Hypertension treatment (same ATC:C02, same generic meaning); see questions on merging. Use when the variable is generic; not for a variable naming one class. T88 rule: ATC:C02 (antihypertensives) is shared by Hypertension treatment, Taking alpha blockers and Taking centrally acting agents. The concept, not the code, tells them apart, and the SOURCE VARIABLE decides the concept: a generic 'blood pressure / hypertension medication' variable is Hypertension treatment only; a variable that names alpha blockers (prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin) is Taking alpha blockers; a variable that names centrally acting agents (clonidine, methyldopa, guanfacine) is Taking centrally acting agents. A generic variable is not evidence of a specific class.
Example source variable description: Current medication for high blood pressure

Concept Description: Participant takes a beta-adrenergic blocking agent (metoprolol, atenolol, propranolol, carvedilol, bisoprolol, nebivolol, labetalol, nadolol, timolol, sotalol). ATC C07A; beta blocker plus diuretic or other combinations (C07B-C07F) count for the beta-blocker component. Counted regardless of indication (hypertension, angina, heart failure, arrhythmia, migraine, tremor). Use when the variable names beta blockers or one of those drugs (FHS also asks about propranolol alone); not for a generic blood pressure medication variable (Hypertension treatment), and not for inhaled beta-AGONISTS (Taking adrenergic bronchodilators). Ophthalmic timolol is not a systemic beta blocker; count it only if the source cannot be told apart. Combination pills: a source variable for 'X with diuretics' counts for X and also for diuretics; production carries the ATC combination code as a variant row.
Example source variable description: ANY BETA BLOCKER|MEDICINE USE: BETA BLOCKERS|Beta Blockers|Beta Blocker Medication Status (Y/N)|BETA-BLOCKERS WITHOUT DIURETICS|Section 9: Medications. Beta blockers [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]

Concept Description: Participant takes a calcium channel blocker: dihydropyridines (amlodipine, nifedipine, felodipine, nicardipine, isradipine, nisoldipine) or non-dihydropyridines (diltiazem, verapamil). ATC C08. Counted regardless of indication (hypertension, angina, arrhythmia). Use when the variable names calcium channel blockers or one of those drugs (CHS and MESA list amlodipine, immediate- and slow-release dihydropyridines, diltiazem and verapamil separately; HCHS lists diltiazem and verapamil); not for a generic blood pressure medication variable (Hypertension treatment). Single-drug variables are written with the ingredient RxNorm code as a variant, so production keeps the drug identity.
Example source variable description: Amlodipine|MEDICINE USE: CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKERS|Calcium Channel Blockers|Diltiazem: 1-Reported Taking diltiazem, 0-Not Exposed|Calcium Channel Blocker Medication Status (Y/N)|AMLODIPINE

Concept Description: Participant takes a centrally acting antihypertensive (clonidine, methyldopa, guanfacine, guanabenz, rauwolfia alkaloids). ATC C02A (antiadrenergic agents, centrally acting). Use when the variable names methyldopa, clonidine or 'centrally acting' agents; not for a generic blood pressure medication variable (Hypertension treatment), not for alpha blockers (Taking alpha blockers), and NOT for 'central nervous system medications' in general - V1 pairs the label 'Central Nervous System medications' with OMOP:21602722, but that code is ATC H02 Corticosteroids for systemic use (the same code V1 gives Taking systemic steroids; Atlas, ATC class concept), so it is not carried here; a CNS-medications group would be far broader than centrally acting antihypertensives. T88 rule: ATC:C02 (antihypertensives) is shared by Hypertension treatment, Taking alpha blockers and Taking centrally acting agents. The concept, not the code, tells them apart, and the SOURCE VARIABLE decides the concept: a generic 'blood pressure / hypertension medication' variable is Hypertension treatment only; a variable that names alpha blockers (prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin) is Taking alpha blockers; a variable that names centrally acting agents (clonidine, methyldopa, guanfacine) is Taking centrally acting agents. A generic variable is not evidence of a specific class. Clonidine is also prescribed for ADHD and withdrawal; counted regardless of indication.
Example source variable description: INTERIM HISTORY OF MEDICINE USED: METHYLDOPA|INTERIM HISTORY OF MEDICINE USED: CLONIDINE|MEDICINE USE: METHYLDOPA

Concept Description: Participant takes a corticosteroid by mouth (prednisone, prednisolone, methylprednisolone, dexamethasone, hydrocortisone). ATC H02A (corticosteroids for systemic use, plain) with route_concept ORAL. Use when the variable says oral steroids / oral corticosteroids; not for inhaled corticosteroids (Taking inhaled corticosteroids), not for topical, nasal or ophthalmic steroids, and not for anabolic or sex steroids. A variable that says only 'steroids' without a route is Taking systemic steroids. Short bursts count as PRESENT only within the variable's own recall window.
Example source variable description: Oral corticosteroids|ORAL STEROIDS

Concept Description: Participant takes an inhaled corticosteroid (budesonide, fluticasone, beclomethasone, mometasone, ciclesonide). ATC R03BA (glucocorticoids, inhalants) with route_concept ENDOTRACHEOPULMONARY. Use when the variable says inhaled steroids / inhaled corticosteroids; not for oral or injected steroids (Taking oral corticosteroids, Taking systemic steroids), not for nasal or topical steroids, A combination inhaler with a long-acting beta-agonist (ICS/LABA, ATC R03AK) does contain an inhaled corticosteroid: production writes it only to Taking adrenergic bronchodilators (ATC:R03AK), but PROPOSED is to emit a record for BOTH concepts so ICS use is not undercounted; see questions.
Example source variable description: Inhaled corticosteroids

Concept Description: Participant takes a diuretic: thiazide (hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, indapamide, metolazone), loop (furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide) or potassium-sparing (amiloride, triamterene, spironolactone), alone or in combination pills. ATC C03. Use when the variable names diuretics or one of those drugs; not for a generic blood pressure medication variable (Hypertension treatment). Spironolactone/eplerenone variables also count for Taking aldosterone receptor blockers, which is the narrower concept. Edge cases: IV diuretics during a hospital stay are a hospital-record exposure, not self-report (see questions on provenance); production also maps a CARDIA item about taking double diuretics to lose weight, which is diuretic misuse rather than treatment (see questions). Combination pills: a source variable for 'X with diuretics' counts for X and also for diuretics; production carries the ATC combination code as a variant row.
Example source variable description: ANY DIURETIC|Thiazide diuretics without k-sparing age|INTERIM HISTORY OF DRUGS TAKEN: DIURETIC, EXAM 6|Diuretics|Diuretic Medication Status (Y/N)|THIAZIDE DIURETICS WITHOUT K-SPARING AGENTS

Concept Description: Participant takes insulin (any type or route: injection, pump). ATC A10A (insulins and analogues); MeSH D007328 is the code most production files use. Use when the variable names insulin; not for oral hypoglycemic agents (Taking oral hypoglycemic agents), not for non-insulin injectables such as GLP-1 agonists (Taking medication for diabetes only), and not for a variable that lumps 'insulin or oral drugs' without separating them (Taking medication for diabetes). Variables differ in time frame (now, last 2 weeks, ever). Insulin concentration in blood is a different concept (MeasurementObservation Insulin in blood).
Example source variable description: Insulins|MEDICINE USE: INSULIN|Diabetes - Insulin TrtSelf (MHEA16C)|Diabetic Insulin Medication Status (Y/N)|INSULINS|Insulin shots now

Concept Description: Participant takes any medication for diabetes or high blood sugar, insulin or non-insulin, as reported by a generic variable ('taking medication to control diabetes'). ATC A10 (drugs used in diabetes). Use when the variable is generic or lumps insulin with pills; not for variables that name only insulin (Taking insulin) or only oral agents (Taking oral hypoglycemic agents). Edge cases: metformin prescribed for prediabetes or PCOS is still counted when the variable cannot tell; ever-versus-current matters ('have you ever taken medication for diabetes' is not current use: PROPOSED reading is HISTORICAL unless a paired variable shows current use; only a current-use answer is PRESENT; production maps such a yes to PRESENT, see questions). Gestational diabetes medication in pregnancy is not distinguished.
Example source variable description: Do you regularly take medication to control diabetes? Q2 [Oral Glucose Tolerance Screening Form, GTSA04. Visit 4]|TAKING MEDS FOR DIABETES|Have you ever taken medication for high blood sugar or diabetes?|Did you take any medication for diabetes or high blood sugar in the past two weeks?|F33 Diabetes Pills|DIABETES: TAKING MEDICINE

Concept Description: Participant takes a lipid-lowering medication that is NOT a statin: fibrates (gemfibrozil, fenofibrate), bile acid sequestrants (cholestyramine, colesevelam), niacin/nicotinic acid, ezetimibe, omega-3 fatty acids, PCSK9 inhibitors and similar. Use when the variable names one of those classes (CHS and MESA ask fibrates, bile-acid sequestrants and niacin separately; FHS 'anti-cholesterol drugs (resins, fibrates, etc.)'; HCHS fibric/nicotinic acids); not for statins (Taking statin medication). TRAP: the code production uses, ATC:C10A, covers ALL lipid-modifying agents INCLUDING statins; it is right only for a variable that says 'lipid-lowering medication' without a class, and such a variable cannot show non-statin use. See questions. PROPOSED: this one concept replaces the two production files tak_nstat_med and taking_non_statin_medication, which carry the same meaning for different cohorts (the V1 list has only tak_nstat_med).
Example source variable description: Bile-acid sequestrants|Fibrates|Niacin and nicotinic acid|ANTI CHOLESTEROL DRUGS (RESINS, FIBRATES, ETC.)|Fibric/Nicotinic Acids (trt of TG and HDL)|TAKEN NIACIN? Q 4

Concept Description: Participant takes an oral blood-glucose-lowering drug: metformin, sulfonylureas (glipizide, glyburide, glimepiride), thiazolidinediones (pioglitazone), DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors. ATC A10B. Use when the variable names oral hypoglycemics / diabetes pills or one of those drugs; not for insulin (Taking insulin) and not for a variable that lumps insulin with pills (Taking medication for diabetes; MESA 'insulin or oral hypoglycemics for diabetes?' is such a lump). Injectable non-insulin drugs (GLP-1 agonists) are in ATC A10B but are not oral; do not count them here. Metformin for prediabetes counts when the variable cannot tell.
Example source variable description: Oral hypoglycemic agents|INTERIM HISTORY OF MEDICINE USED: ORAL HYPOGLYCEMIC AGENTS|ORAL HYPOGLYCEMIC AGENTS-NOW CONTRUCTED FROM:

Concept Description: Participant takes an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, pravastatin, lovastatin, fluvastatin, pitavastatin). ATC C10AA. Statin plus ezetimibe or other combinations count for the statin component. Use when the variable names statins or one of those drugs (ARIC 'statin use in the past 2 weeks', FHS 'anti-cholesterol drugs (statins, e.g. lovastatin, pravastatin)', JHS statin status); not for non-statin lipid drugs (Taking non statin medication). Generic variables ('any lipid-lowering medication', 'taking meds for high cholesterol', CARDIA 'currently taking cholesterol medication') do not prove statin use: production maps some to the broader ATC:C10A as a variant, which is not statin-specific. See questions.
Example source variable description: Statin use in the past 2 weeks based on 2004 medication codes [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]|MEDICATION USE: ANTI CHOLESTEROL DRUGS (STATINS -- E.G. LOVASTATIN, PRAVASTATIN)|Statin Medication Status (Y/N)|Self-Reported Statin Medication Status (Y/N)

Concept Description: Participant takes a systemic (oral, injected or IV) corticosteroid, as reported by a variable that says only 'steroids' or 'glucocorticosteroid' without a route. ATC H02A. Use when the route is unspecified or covers oral and injected use; not for inhaled, nasal, topical or ophthalmic steroids (Taking inhaled corticosteroids is the inhaled concept), and not for anabolic or sex steroids. A variable that says oral steroids is Taking oral corticosteroids, the narrower concept. WHI 'oral daily use of a glucocorticosteroid' is mapped here in production although it names the oral route (see questions).
Example source variable description: USING STEROIDS? Q 15|F44 Oral daily use of a glucocorticosteroid

Concept Description: Participant takes a direct or peripheral vasodilator: hydralazine, minoxidil, nitrates (isosorbide, nitroglycerin), nitroprusside, other peripheral vasodilators. ATC C04 (peripheral vasodilators) for the group, but hydralazine is C02DB, minoxidil C02DC and nitroprusside C02DD (arteriolar smooth muscle agents, C02D; verified in RxNav RxClass 2026-10-04), organic nitrates are C01DA, and the CHS/MESA 'vasodilators with diuretics' group is C02L. Use when the variable names vasodilators or one of those drugs (CHS/MESA: 'peripheral vasodilators, exclude dipyridamole', 'vasodilators, a mixed group'; FHS: hydralazine, Minipres, minoxidil); not for ACE inhibitors, calcium channel blockers or alpha blockers, which also dilate vessels but have their own concepts. Nitrates for angina count here, so this concept mixes antihypertensive and antianginal use (see questions).
